_comment: Curated source of truth for the station/destination registry (TERC-46). The TERC report API provides names and activity; it provides NO coordinates (confirmed TERC-79 by reading the report Lambdas' own field lists) — those live here. TERC-79 reconciled three sources: TERC's own production real-time app, an older legacy station table, and OSM geocoding. Every coordinate is checked against OpenStreetMap's Lake Tahoe polygon and sits in open water; `source` records which won. `verified` still means confirmed by TERC staff for THIS project (none yet). ALL coordinates are stored at exactly 5 decimal places — see _precision.
_precision: 5 decimal places everywhere, deliberately and uniformly. At Lake Tahoe's latitude 1 degree of longitude is 86.4 km, so a coordinate rounded to 2 dp carries +/-432 m of slop and 3 of these 18 stations land on dry ground; 5 dp is +/-0.4 m. Mixed precision was the TERC-79 bug: 11 of 18 markers rendered on land. Do not 'tidy' trailing zeros away — 39.23640 must keep its zero so the column stays uniform and the class of bug cannot return.
_station_names: Names are the report API's own Station_Name values, read from GET /report/ns-stations (TERC-79). Ids 1, 3, 5 and 10 were previously placeholders ('NS Station N') — they are really Cascade, Glenbrook, Meeks and Camp Richardson. Getting id 3's name right matters: it is Glenbrook, on the EAST shore, and it had been sitting 19 km away on the south-west.

stations.name: Cascade
stations.note: NOT in the scientist's site list; last reading 2017-11-20. On CASCADE LAKE, not Lake Tahoe — TERC's nearshore page describes the network as ten Tahoe stations plus one on Cascade Lake. Looks decommissioned; position geocoded.

stations.name: Dollar Point
stations.source: legacy table (app value is 542 m offshore, vs 2.0 m reported depth)
stations.note: WORKING (scientist, Sep 2026). Legacy coordinate, 83 m offshore. The production app's 39.1947,-120.089 is 542 m out, which does not square with the 2.0 m depth this station reports.

stations.name: Glenbrook
stations.note: Scientist: 'thought it was working, but it seems something happened'. Last reading 2022-08-26. EAST shore — was 'NS Station 3' at 38.933,-120.025, 19 km away on the south-west.

stations.name: Homewood
stations.source: legacy table (app value is 1.1 km north)
stations.note: WORKING (scientist, Sep 2026). Legacy coordinate, 12 m offshore, matching its 2.0 m reported depth. Sits exactly on the 39.09 N midline the half-lake destinations split on — counted as north.

stations.name: Meeks
stations.note: NOT in the scientist's site list; last reading 2020-10-22. Looks decommissioned. Position is Meeks Bay, 72 m offshore — geocoded best effort, unconfirmed.

stations.name: Rubicon
stations.note: Reporting live. Absent from the scientist's list of 9, but he states there are 10 live NS sites — Rubicon is the tenth. Sits on the pier, which is why OSM tiles render its pixel as land.

stations.name: Sand Harbor
stations.note: Scientist: removed due to CONSTRUCTION at its location; redeploy planned for the fall. Still transmitting rows, but every water field is null — barometric only. (Our old note said 'dark since Q4 2024'; it is transmitting, just not water data.)

stations.name: Tahoe City
stations.source: derived — BOTH sources on dry land, 2.1 km apart
stations.note: Scientist: damaged/out of lake, awaiting a new sensor from the manufacturer. Last reading 2026-01-16. BOTH coordinate sources put this on land, 2.1 km apart — derived from the OSM village centre, 73 m offshore. Needs TERC.

stations.name: Camp Richardson
stations.note: Scientist: damaged/out of lake. Last reading 2025-04-22 — so NOT 'never observed 2024-2026' as we previously recorded. Was 'NS Station 10' at 38.99,-120.105, 880 m inland and 7 km north-west.

stations.name: Timber Cove
stations.source: derived from the Timber Cove Lodge pier — legacy inland, app 292 m out
stations.note: Scientist: in-water sensors are OUT OF THE WATER due to damage — 'any data that comes through is just atmospheric pressure'. Also drops out for a day or two when the cellular network is busy, mostly over holidays. Water fields are currently all null. Derived from the Timber Cove Lodge pier, 72 m offshore.

stations.name: Cedar Point
stations.note: Scientist: damaged/out of lake ('possible that the site is experiencing issues'). Still transmitting, water fields all null. WEST shore, between Tahoe City and Homewood — the old placeholder put it on the east shore, which is why it had been grouped under the Glenbrook destination.

stations.name: USCG 2020 Met Station
stations.note: Status unknown — the nearshore scientist does not control the met stations or their API calls; referred to another scientist, no answer yet.

stations.name: NASA Buoy TB2
stations.note: Silent since 2026-08-12. Status unknown — referred to another scientist, no answer yet.

stations.name: Homewood TC
stations.note: Id-less endpoint. Scientist: a CHAIN with temperature sensors at several depths, a dissolved-oxygen sensor at the bottom and a pressure sensor — its own table, separate from the nearshore stations. Currently OUT OF THE WATER due to damage. 584 m offshore, deeper water than the dock-mounted sensors, as expected.

_destinations_comment: Station membership recomputed in TERC-79 by nearest destination, using the corrected coordinates. Two groupings had been artefacts of wrong coordinates: 'glenbrook' held station 12 (Cedar Point, actually WEST shore) instead of station 3 (Glenbrook, 0.1 km away), and 'tahoe-keys' held station 3. The half-lake destinations keep the documented rule — split at 39.09 N, the lake's E-W midline. Note Glenbrook (39.08830) falls 0.2 km SOUTH of that line, so it groups with South Lake Tahoe by the rule.
_tiebreaker: The app and the legacy table disagree by up to 2.1 km. Tiebreaker: every station that reports a depth reports 1.4-2.0 m (Depth_m4C_Avg), i.e. sensors on private docks in shallow water. So where sources conflict, take the in-water candidate CLOSEST to shore and reject any candidate on land. Result: every nearshore station now sits 12-134 m offshore. Disagreements still worth TERC's confirmation: Dollar Point (sources 1232 m apart), Homewood (1139 m), Rubicon (516 m), Timber Cove (374 m), Tahoe City (2111 m, and BOTH sources are on dry land).
_status_source: Station status below is from a TERC scientist's email (Sep 2026), answering the station roll-call. It supersedes our earlier guesses. Two things it settles: (a) the API's Station_Name values ARE the names to show the public ('my recollection is that the API returns data based on station name'), and every name he lists matches the /report/ns-stations roster exactly; (b) he identifies 9 sites by name and states there are 10 live NS sites — the missing one is Rubicon, which is reporting live. He does not mention Cascade or Meeks at all; those two last reported in 2017 and 2020 and look decommissioned. NOTE he does not recognise stations by id, only by name, so never ask him an id-keyed question.
